novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 / comparator promise to NabiGuoLiu2026
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed strict sharpening is only the tautological decomposition obtained after defining Delta as K∩Lambda⊥; no theorem yet supplies a non-definitional frontier or strict comparison against the anchor's multi-constraint result.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition 1 (two-verma-kill-test)
novelty_flags.one_line: The anchor already exhibits a second-order solution h for the sequential two-Verma constraints and says this completes the reverse direction, so recasting that same witness as Delta=0 is not a new proposition.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 (compatibility-frontier)
soundness_flags.one_line: Given Lambda⊆K and S=K⊥, Lambda⊥=S⊕(K∩Lambda⊥) and the Delta=0 iff Lambda=K clause are Hilbert-space decomposition identities after the proposal defines Delta to be that residual space.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2 (split-regularity)
soundness_flags.one_line: Its asserted positive inf-sup modulus and “stable compatible decomposition” are neither defined objects nor quantified conclusions, so the theorem does not state a testable mathematical result beyond the submanifold implication.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 (angle-aware-limit)
soundness_flags.one_line: The triangular statement uses Delta(P_n), D_eff at P_n, and projectors Q_j at P_n although these are defined only at P; it also concludes consistency of an undefined “plug-in variance.”

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 4 (angle-aware-limit)
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The inference result is conditional on zero compatibility defect and on the displayed sieve, learned-projector, and nuisance remainder controls.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Asymptotic normality and efficiency attainment only UNDER an indexed zero-defect condition and primitive conditions that imply b_n+q_n^{m_n}+delta_n(1-q_n^{m_n})/(1-q_n)=o_P(1) and sqrt(n)r_n=o_P(1).

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 17–18, Proposition 3 and Remark 5; pp. 78–81, Appendix S4.2, equations (S46)–(S51) and the solution immediately following (S51)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves only a residual-span inclusion and conjectures general completeness, but for its sequential two-Verma example it explicitly solves (S51) for a valid second-order perturbation h and states that this completes the reverse direction.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 6–7, Theorem 3 and discussion immediately following it
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3 concerns general Markov models defined by conditional-independence constraints; the paper states that an exact projection onto the general model orthocomplement and the exact efficient influence function remain open.
For known closed subspaces, cyclic products have a quick-uniform versus arbitrarily-slow dichotomy; Theorem 4.4 gives a quantitative uniform rate under a generalized Friedrichs number below one.

The paper supplies influence-function-based estimators and efficiency results for identified effects in hidden-variable graphical models, providing a valid baseline causal-inference comparator but not a multi-Verma tangent-completeness theorem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the Delta-defined headline with an independently checkable condition stated in observable/fixing primitives, then prove that it is sufficient (and, if possible, necessary on a named graph class) for Lambda=K; make this the comparison to NabiGuoLiu2026.

Remove the sequential two-Verma proposition as a novelty claim, or use the anchor’s explicit h construction only as a sanity reduction while proving a genuinely new graph class beyond that worked example.

Index every geometric object by P_n and state primitive sieve approximation, projector-estimation, nuisance-rate, variance-estimator, and moment assumptions from which the displayed remainder and Wald conclusion are derived.
Position the estimator result against HristachePatilea2016 and provide either a strict rate/assumption improvement or a fully specified efficiency-attaining estimator under the new fixing geometry.

recommended_next_step: Revise around a non-definitional multi-constraint completeness criterion and a fully indexed primitive inference theorem; do not advance the present field-tier core to Stage 0.
